en.title: End of Abyss Developers Detail Crafting an Industrial World Ripe for Exploration
en.summary: Section 9 Interactive has offered a deeper look into the creation of their upcoming action-adventure title, **End of Abyss**. Developers are focusing on making their meticulously crafted industrial environments a joy to explore, filled with secrets for players to uncover.
en.body:
The eerie, industrial depths of **End of Abyss** are taking shape, and developer Section 9 Interactive, with publisher Epic Games, has pulled back the curtain a bit further. A new behind-the-scenes trailer dives into the nitty-gritty of world-building and level design, revealing how the team is striving to make exploration not just a means to an end, but a core, compelling part of the experience. This upcoming action-adventure title, set to launch on October 1, 2026, promises an atmospheric horror journey where every nook and cranny might hold a secret.

Level designer Robin Jansson articulated the delicate balance the team is trying to strike. "As the designer, I want the world to make sense. But I also want you to explore – we want you to explore. So, there’s a bit of a fine line there you have to tread to make it fantastical while still understandable," Jansson explained. This philosophy directly influences the game's environmental layout, particularly in the ways secrets are embedded. "So, nooks and crannies are great for me as a designer because that’s where I hide the secrets. So, I design a lot of those, I would say. I think it’s quite important for the genre. In a Metroidvania, you want a lot of hidden nooks, hidden stuff."

## Crafting an Industrial Labyrinth

The world of **End of Abyss** is predominantly man-made, a stark industrial landscape featuring metal, concrete, and machinery. Yet, the developers are working to imbue these sterile environments with a sense of organic decay and intrigue. Even areas resembling sewers are being given a touch of life through thoughtful wear-and-tear. "Basically, everything is man-made in there, I would say. It’s a very industrial sort of environment. There’s a lot of metal and concrete, machinery and pipes, all sorts of things that you would expect in a factory-like environment," Jansson noted. The key to achieving this organic feel, even within artificial structures, lies in subtle details. "Having holes in it or broken railings is going to feel a lot more organic."

## Rewarding the Curious Explorer

This focus on exploration and hidden secrets is a cornerstone of the **End of Abyss** experience, particularly for fans of the Metroidvania genre. The game aims to reward players not just through combat prowess, but through diligent investigation and careful play. Progression is tied to upgraded gear and new equipment, encouraging players to delve into every corner of the map. This approach ensures that the journey through the game's unsettling environments is as engaging as the narrative itself, fostering a sense of discovery that keeps players invested. The deliberate design choices in level architecture underscore the game's commitment to making the world itself a central character and a constant source of intrigue.

## What's Next

With the launch date of October 1, 2026, drawing closer, **End of Abyss** is set to release on PC via the Epic Games Store, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. Pre-orders are currently available, and Section 9 Interactive has indicated that their behind-the-scenes series will continue weekly until the game's release.

content_raw: Developer Section 9 Interactive and publisher Epic Games have released a new trailer for the action-adventure game End of Abyss . The trailer, which you can check out below, gives us a behind-the-scenes look at how the development team designed the game’s world in order to make exploration fun for players. Level designer Robin Jansson spoke about this, noting that “As the designer, I want the world to make sense. But I also want you to explore – we want you to explore. So, there’s a bit of a fine line there you have to tread to make it fantastical while still understandable.” Jansson went on to talk about how the level design in End of Abyss hides plenty of secrets. “So, nooks and crannies are great for me as a designer because that’s where I hide the secrets. So, I design a lot of those, I would say. I think it’s quite important for the genre. In a Metroidvania, you want a lot of hidden nooks, hidden stuff.” He went on to discuss the style of level design employed in End of Abyss , which involved bringing an industrial setting to life. Jansson spoke about how the team went about creating plenty of variety despite areas largely featuring pipes and metal, and how even sewer-like spaces can be made to feel more organic by adding some wear-and-tear to the surroundings. “Basically, everything is man-made in there, I would say. It’s a very industrial sort of environment. There’s a lot of metal and concrete, machinery and pipes, all sorts of things that you would expect in a factory-like environment. Some sections of the game are more in a sewer-like space; some are a bit more broken than others, which makes them feel a bit more organic, even though it is metal we’re still talking about. Having holes in it or broken railings is going to feel a lot more organic. And there are organic elements as well, but usually those come after the catastrophe of the game.” Environment artist Gustav Bunse also spoke about the art that went into creating the world of End of Abyss , noting that plenty of fantasy and sci-fi elements were involved in the creation of the game. “It’s much easier to make it feel man-made,” he said. The commentary by the development team is broken up by gameplay segments showcasing the various aspects they are discussing, such as the title’s metroidvania aspects where players can come across weak walls that can be blown up by using explosive charges, opening up new zones ripe for exploration in the process. End of Abyss is being developed for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S, and is slated for release on October 1st. The PC version will only be available through the Epic Games Store. The title’s release date was announced during Summer Game Fest 2026, with a trailer showcasing some of the tense, exploration-focused gameplay that emphasizes the player’s various tools and the game’s challenges, which will also involve resource scarcity.
